description: §19.4.3 + §13.2 — a CELL-assigned failable SERVER call, `@out = risky(2) !{ | .Boom(m) :> { …; return } }`. The stub answers the Boom error envelope, so the arm runs and its `return` returns from the AUTHOR's function `load`: the statement after the handler (`@after = "ran"`) never runs and @out keeps its prior value (the error envelope never lands in the cell). The pre-fix emit wrapped the call + handler in a detached async IIFE, so the arm's `return` only left the IIFE and `@after = "ran"` executed anyway (g-failable-cell-load-fire-and-forget-stale-read-dead-return; S435 ruling: lift).
rationale: §19.4.3: the `!{}` handler's arm runs in the enclosing function's control flow, so a terminal `return` in an arm is the early-return-on-error idiom and exits that function. §13.2 SHALL insert `await` at the server call site and sequence dependent operations, so the handler decision is made on the RESOLVED envelope before the next statement runs.
